idea.title: Unknown portals are ordinary explore frontier at any round, priced like unseen ground, with the landing risk this dragon has seen and the time left to rejoin the king
idea.hypothesis: sig, 2026-09-29: "What if there's a map with a super windy path with no portal there but then alternative is a portal straight to a feeding ground. I think we should always explore unexplored portals and I don't agree with only doing it when no other option" and "Tho obviously in the portal map the snakes will die". General quantity: steps to the next pearls eaten by a dragon whose best explore choice is an unknown portal, against its best known-ground choice, and the length that crossing costs (landing deaths within 10 rounds, and length that can no longer reach the king at the fold). Today targets.hpp chooseExplore takes an unknown portal only when no never-seen or stale tile is reachable, and scoring.hpp charges any other unknown-portal step -P.unknownPortalPenalty, so a long winding walk always beats a short portal. Evidence: E0284 (I812 with I709 merged, portal frontier from the start plus a sonar-pooled back-off, -9 over 720) lost on near_portals (0.432 over 33) and near_autarky; its post-mortem found the cost was length stranded in other rooms at the fold (our longest trailed in 11 of 14 games reaching r499, p 0.029, total length level), and its back-off reached few dragons. E0283 (I247) was level; E0054 (I094) +0.9 on an old champion; leaders cross from r8-10 (audit 1790610131755582000 A1, p 2e-7). E0287 (I446, kept on judgement) already sends dragons out of portal-only rooms. Options: (1) this idea, the portal as ordinary frontier with its landing risk and fold guard; (2) a crossing gate imitating the top three teams (I849); (3) I828's door priced by what the seen ends lead to. This is (1), each part behind its own switch: (1) an unknown portal edge in the dragon's region is a frontier candidate scored like an unseen tile (its far side counted as unseen), ranked with every other frontier by the same path-distance score, at any round; (2) its landing risk: each dragon keeps the crossings it has seen this game (its own and teammates' in view) and whether the crosser died or was shut in within 10 rounds, and charges an unknown portal that expected loss (a prior from E0284's measured 38.8% bad on near_portals, updated by what it sees), so on a deadly portal map it backs off by itself; (3) the fold guard: no crossing whose way back to the king's reported area (over the portal pairs known) doesn't fit the rounds left before the fold. Measure first on the champion (shadow copy): how often (1) changes the explore pick per style (near_portals, near_trauma, portalrooms, near_autarky, worldgen, eval) and the path steps saved; stop only if the upper bound of changed picks is below 0.1 a game on every portal style. Circumstance for the judge, declared now: portal maps (near_portals, near_trauma, portalrooms, official Portals and Trauma); sig's portal rule applies (level or better there, no loss elsewhere). Report each switch's share of the result.

idea.title: Quick fix of E0309: The seen-exit split rule binds only on a dragon's first turn: from its second turn the parent has moved its tail on
idea.hypothesis: E0309's coder built this fix in its follow-on turn (E0309: kept, SPRT accepted, est +5.2). Defect: P.splitExitMustBeSeen held splits past a dragon's first turn whose unseen tail exit was free: 0 of 71 such holds had a body there (17 of 56 E0309 games, 60 on Portals/Trauma copies), against 126 of 136 first-turn holds (n = 56, p = 0.0006). Fetch it and cherry-pick only its commits: `git fetch -q --no-tags /Users/me/Dev/unsw-battlecode-2026 fix/E0309 && git cherry-pick 11bd366feb56ae925c13f2523c0be3edab7be85b..FETCH_HEAD`; resolve any conflict keeping both the fix and the champion's change, rerun the bot tests and the quick check, and change nothing else. Its coder's reasoning: Quick fix on E0309 (I633, kept H1 +5.2): P.splitExitMustBeSeen holds an ordinary split whose child's only free tail exits were never in this dragon's view. General quantity: splits the rule holds whose unseen exit was really free, per game. Its reason (a newborn's tail touches its parent's body just out of view) holds only on the dragon's first turn: the parent has a lower id, so before the child's second turn it has moved its tail on or died. Measured on E0309's 56 candidate-v-champion games (Autarky, Dilemma, Portals and Trauma copies, sprint and worldgen maps; replay truth at each held turn): 126 of 136 first-turn holds had a body on every unseen tail exit, 0 of 71 later holds did (95% 0-5%, 17 games; rates_p 5e-45; were even 10% of later holds real saves, 0 of 71 happens by luck 6e-4). The later holds are young long children (ages 1-3, 5-7 long, whose tail still sits where they were born): 60 of 71 on Portals/Trauma copies (5 a game there), 7 in 16 worldgen games, 4 on Autarky. Each delays a split whose child would have lived. Change (committed 7f9737c): the rule binds only when w.round == w.firstRound (the process's first turn); no new number. In 34 fix-v-kept games (Portals, Trauma, Autarky copies, 8 fresh worldgen) the fix made none of the kept's 68 later holds (59 on Portals/Trauma, 12 games) and first-turn children dying at birth into a body stayed level (fix 11, kept 13; sign 3 v 4). Scenarios: a 5-7-long child 1-3 rounds old at a corridor end on Portals splits when its only free tail exit is unseen; a newborn at the same spot still doesn't. Choices: scope = the ordinary split's exit test; trigger = the process's first turn, observed (firstRound), not a round count; left out: round-0 starters are first-turn too (2 holds in 56 games, both free exits, kept for their unseen teammates' bodies). Options: (1) narrow the rule to the first turn (this; removes 34% of its changed decisions, all false holds); (2) remember bodies seen out of view (I274), which would also fix later unseen-body exits but none were measured here; (3) drop the rule on non-sprint maps by map style, a bare condition the bot can't observe, rejected. E0309's own SPRT: sprint-style trials 0.522 (z 3.9, n 601), worldgen 0.496 (z -0.7, n 577), others 0.504 (z 0.9); the opponent screen tilted negative on general maps (pooled z about -2.2), where these later holds fall.

idea.title: Measure first whether explored tie-breaks give the value net a move ranking: a logging copy plays the other safe step on a hashed share of tied turns
idea.hypothesis: sig's value-net line (I842, 2026-09-29, run outside the queue at his exception). General quantity: on turns where 2+ steps scoring.hpp calls safe tie on score (15,143 of 93,632 such turns in 260 logging games, about 58 a game), the line and team length change over 10 and 50 rounds, and tools/value.py's win-chance change, after the net's pick against the champion's. Why: I842's net (tools/valuenet_fit.py on branch orch/valuenet, 573k rows: our 1,484 online games, 260 champion logging games, 2,105 leaders' ranked games; decoy check dropped cheji's and calc's unranked games) ranks the played step no better than the champion's score (rank correlation 0.178 v 0.203 generated, 0.175 v 0.152 off-generator) and fits no better than ridge regression (pooled per-official-map +0.024 MSE, 95% +0.012 to +0.035); on-policy rows never show the steps the champion doesn't take, so its 89% disagreement on ties carries a predicted edge of only +0.05 length. Options: (1) explore on ties with fit.py's EXPLORE_CPP draw (20% of tied turns, every dragon), fit the net's move part on explored turns, then run it as a tie-breaker on ties only as its own SPRT (this idea is (1)'s measurement); (2) the linear model instead, equal on every held-out check and readable (1,116 weights); (3) neither: the portal-crossing gap (leaders cross 32-40% of turns an open portal step exists, per game, v ours 17-22%) stays with I828, I848 and I849, since neither team's crossings show a 10-round gain. Choices: tied turns only (ties carry 16% of the 2+-safe turns and leave out margins above 0); every dragon; horizons 10 and 50; a label linked to the win (value.py) beside the length ones. Measured circumstance: ties, 58 a game. Stop only if the net's explored picks do worse than the champion's picks at chance.paired_z per game <= -1.28 (p <= 0.1), on both our generator's maps and off-generator maps (worldgen plus renamed official copies), read apart; otherwise build (1).
